# S1 · The problem

**You speak first. 0:00 to 1:20. Slide 1, then slide 2's top line.**

Your job: make the room feel the problem before anyone explains a solution. If you do this well, everything the other five say lands. If you open with statistics, it does not.

Nobody is judging your English. They are judging whether you understood the problem. Speak slowly.

---

## 1 · What you say, word for word

Learn the shape, not the exact words. Look at the panel, not the screen.

> "Good morning. We are team Davinciable, and our problem statement is 26104: real-time detection and prevention of voice cloning impersonation attacks.
>
> *(pause)*
>
> AI voices have stopped sounding like robots. Today, a few seconds of anyone's voice, from an Instagram reel or a WhatsApp voice note, is enough to make that voice say anything you type.
>
> So imagine your phone rings, and it is your father's voice. He sounds stressed. He needs money right now, or he needs an OTP. **You have no way to tell whether that is really him.** Not by listening. The voice is perfect.
>
> *(pause, let it sit)*
>
> That is the problem in one sentence. **The human ear has stopped being proof of identity, and everything we do on the phone still assumes that it is.**
>
> The same call reaches a company's finance desk in the CFO's voice, and there the transfer has six more zeros on it.
>
> And nothing we already have helps. Caller ID can be faked. Calling back does not help if the attacker controls the number. And 'I know his voice' is exactly the thing being attacked.
>
> The problem statement asks for five things, and most teams will build only the first. Detect **during the call**, not on a recording afterwards. Give a **risk score you can act on**, not just a label. **Prevent** the transaction, not just report it. Run **on the device**, so no audio ever leaves the building. And work in **Indian languages** over **real phone lines**.
>
> Our answer is called Pramaan, which means proof. The idea in one line: **the voice is never the last factor.** Pramaan listens to the live call, scores it every half second, and holds the money until something that is not the voice says yes."

**Hand over:** "S2 will show you what we built."

---

## 2 · Why we open this way

Every other team will open with a news statistic about deepfake fraud. The panel will hear that opening eight times before lunch.

We open with a phone call the judges can imagine receiving themselves. It costs nothing and it makes them lean in. Then we widen it to the bank, because that is who actually pays for the product, and the judges know it.

The rule: **do not sell the solution in your slot.** Your only job is to make them want the answer. S2 gives it.

---

## 3 · Every word you will say, explained

You will not be asked to define these, but if you stumble on one it shows. Know them.

| word | full form | what it means in one line |
|---|---|---|
| **AI** | artificial intelligence | software that learns patterns from examples instead of following written rules |
| **voice cloning** | | making software copy one specific person's voice, from a short sample |
| **deepfake** | | any media generated by AI to look or sound like a real person |
| **impersonation attack** | | pretending to be someone else to make a victim act |
| **OTP** | one-time password | the code your bank sends to your phone |
| **CFO** | chief financial officer | the person who controls a company's money |
| **caller ID** | caller identification | the number that shows on your screen; it can be forged |
| **spoofing** | | faking the number so the call looks like it comes from someone you trust |
| **on the device** | | the software runs on the bank's own computer, and no audio is sent to the internet |
| **risk score** | | a number from 0 to 1 saying how likely this voice is machine-made |
| **SIH** | Smart India Hackathon | this event |
| **PS** | problem statement | the problem we picked, number 26104 |
| **Pramaan** | प्रमाण | Hindi and Sanskrit for "proof". We chose it because proof, not suspicion, is the product |

---

## 4 · The numbers you own

You only need three, and you say them slowly.

| number | when you say it |
|---|---|
| **a few seconds** of someone's voice is enough to clone it | in the opening |
| **five** things the problem statement asks for | when you list them |
| **{{min_commit}} seconds** is how fast we answer | only if you have time; otherwise leave it to S2 |

Everything else belongs to someone else. If a judge asks you an accuracy question during your slot, say: **"S4 has those numbers and will cover them in a moment."** That is a correct, confident answer, not a dodge.

---

## 5 · Questions you may get, and your answers

**"Is this actually happening in India, or is it theoretical?"**
> "It is happening. Voice cloning tools are free or a few hundred rupees a month, and they need only a few seconds of audio, which almost everyone has posted publicly. Our project does not depend on any one fraud statistic; it depends on the fact that the technology is now cheap, easy and good, which anyone can verify in ten minutes."

**"Why voice? Why not video deepfakes?"**
> "Because voice is the one that is already inside every workflow. Banks, offices and families all act on phone calls today, with no verification step at all. Video calls at least make people suspicious. A phone call does not."

**"Who exactly is your user?"**
> "Bank and NBFC contact centres and treasury desks first, because they carry the fraud losses and the compliance requirement. Then company finance teams. Then telecom operators. The same system protects an ordinary person, but the buyer is the institution."
> (NBFC = non-banking financial company, like Bajaj Finance or Muthoot.)

**"Isn't this a solved problem? Doesn't the bank already verify?"**
> "They verify the number and sometimes an OTP. Neither of those checks whether the voice on the call is a real human. That is the exact gap, and it is the one our system fills."

---

## 6 · What not to say

- **Do not quote a fraud loss figure in crores.** We have not verified one, and a judge who has will remember it.
- **Do not say "99% accurate"** or any accuracy number at all. That is S4's slot and our real numbers are more interesting than a round one.
- **Do not say "unfortunately" or "we could not".** Nothing in your slot is an apology.
- **Do not run over 1:20.** If you feel late, cut the CFO sentence and go straight to the five requirements.

---

## 7 · Your checklist before you speak

- [ ] You know the five requirements in order: during the call, actionable score, prevention, on-device, Indian languages.
- [ ] You can say "the human ear has stopped being proof of identity" without reading it.
- [ ] You have practised the two pauses. They are what make it land.
- [ ] You know your handover line and you say the next person's name.
